conversation.content:
Hi there, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your baby has arrived. I’ll be using a short, well-studied questionnaire called the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s simply a way to hear, in your words, how things have been going emotionally over the past week. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me there’s an immediate safety concern, and there’s no judgment—just support. We’ll walk through ten gentle questions together; you can answer in whatever way feels most comfortable. Ready to start?

First, I’d love to know: in the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt hard to do?

Hi, Maya… thanks for having me. 

I can still laugh, but it feels kind of muted—like even when something’s funny, the giggle fades pretty fast and I’m back to feeling “blah.” Before the baby I’d really belly-laugh at silly stuff, but this week it’s been more of a quiet chuckle, if that makes sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah, I can still laugh, but it feels kind of muted—like even when something’s funny, the giggle fades pretty fast and I’m back to feeling “blah.” Before the baby I’d really belly-laugh at silly stuff, but this week it’s been more of a quiet chuckle, if that makes sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like when my mom comes over or when I get to take the baby for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of the big, happy buzz I felt before.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week I caught myself thinking, “I should’ve done this better,” especially when the baby was fussy at 3 a.m. I know rationally it’s not my fault, but the thought still pops up—like I’m not quite measuring up as a mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes my mind just races—like I’ll suddenly worry the baby isn’t breathing even though I can see her chest moving. It doesn’t last long; I can usually talk myself down, but those little spikes of worry come out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had full panic, but there’ve been a couple moments—like when I’m alone at night—where my chest feels tight and I think, “What if I can’t handle this?” It passes quickly, maybe a minute or two, but it’s unsettling while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

A few days this week it’s felt like the dishes, laundry, and feedings just pile up faster than I can manage. I usually push through, but by dinner time I’m exhausted and teary, thinking “I can’t keep up,” even though I know it’s normal new-mom stuff.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m pretty tired by evening, so I fall asleep okay. Once in a while I’ll lie there running through the day’s “should-haves,” but mostly I drift off within ten minutes. I only woke up extra early one night because the baby stirred and then my mind started ticking.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I do feel kind of down some parts of the day—like a heavy, gray cloud that comes and goes. It’s not all day, but I’ll catch myself sighing for no reason or just feeling empty while I’m folding onesies. I cried twice this week when it hit harder, but I can still smile at the baby, so it’s not totally hopeless—just... sad.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when the baby wouldn’t settle and once when I dropped a plate and felt like the world’s clumsiest mom. It wasn’t all-day sobbing, more like sudden tears that stopped after a few minutes, but yeah, the sadness definitely spilled over.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother (1 week pp)  
Date: ___  
Instrument: EPDS-10 (patient-verbal format)

Areas endorsed above threshold/at-risk (score ≥1):

<sym>Low mood, anhedonia, excessive self-blame, intrusive worries, brief panic-like episodes, feeling overwhelmed, tearfulness</sym>

Pattern Summary  
- Persistent “blah” mood with intermittent tearfulness; pleasure blunted but not absent  
- Daily unhelpful cognitions (“not measuring up”) and situational guilt  
- Multiple unprovoked anxious thoughts + nocturnal chest tightness/“can’t handle this” fear  
- Functional impact: difficulty keeping up with chores, end-of-day tearfulness and fatigue  
- Sleep initiation preserved; one early-morning rumination episode  
- No self-harm ideation (endorsed 0)

Screening Significance  
- Meets provisional cut-off for possible minor-moderate <med>postpartum depression</med> and co-occurring <med>anxiety</med>  
- Protective factors: social support (mother visits), ability to enjoy some activities, no safety concerns

Recommendation: Continue monitoring with formal EPDS scoring; consider referral for further evaluation and supportive counseling. Safety plan reviewed—return sooner if worsening mood, panic, or any self-harm thoughts.
